title: Nick Baltas talks Signal Strength, Trend Following & Portfolio Strategies - Systematic Investor 295

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Nick Baltas talks Signal Strength, Trend Following & Portfolio Strategies - Systematic Investor 295.docx

speakers: Neils Kostrup Larsen (host, hedge fund manager)
summary: May 2024 Systematic Investor episode: Baltas answers listener questions on agnostic risk parity, equal risk allocation across asset classes, ideal trend allocation and volatility regimes, then summarises his FT piece on equity momentum crowding (party and hangover analogy). Conclusion: fixed risk budgets embed return bets; dynamic allocation and vol scaling manage momentum crash risk.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: one of the largest negative contributors in a trend following strategy that is CA right
claims.claim: Cocoa was historically one of the largest negative contributors to trend following, yet its 2024 rally helped, which defends holding markets that have never trended well.
claims.conditions: cocoa trends only occasionally; benefit arrives unannounced

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: we were trying to be agnostic to the underperformer in some respect because at the end of the day you also play the diversification game
claims.claim: Trend portfolios should include markets without screening out past underperformers, because diversification means unpredictable markets sometimes deliver the big trends.
claims.testable: partly - compare screened vs unscreened universes

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: persistent Trends not necessarily in a way that we can forecast but certainly by putting them in portfolio we can achieve to to diversify away but also capture those returns
claims.claim: In 2024 trends appeared in markets not historically big drivers (cocoa, equities); one cannot forecast which, so breadth is the way to capture them.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: this Equity Market rally specific speically on those AI names and this Equity momentum kind of driving prices higher and higher and higher
claims.claim: AI-stock equity momentum has pushed prices up and raises concern that the trade is overcrowded.
claims.testable: no - opinion on crowding, no measure given

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: some of the sectors that we would think would be great for Trend because they're liquid like currencies like equities have not necessarily been that great to trade from a trend following perspective
claims.claim: Liquid currency and equity index markets have been poor trend sectors because of quick corrections, while energies trended better over the last 10 to 15 years.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: replication is dependent upon its success to replicate by nature but also it's dependent the success of the underlying instrument we're trying to replicate
claims.claim: A replication product can only perform if the CTA strategy it copies performs, and replicating faster programs is harder because of style drift and repositioning.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I see the value of grouping together uh investment profiles and then trying to find a way to achieve that in an efficient manner with a limited set of markets
claims.claim: Replication can capture broad macro trends efficiently with a limited market set (10 to 40 markets), though how many are enough is debated.
claims.testable: partly - tracking error vs number of markets

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: it is how closely can you actually track the thing you're trying to replicate that to me is quite important
claims.claim: High daily correlation is not the same as matching performance: replicators can track closely then underperform and later outperform, so lower fees do not guarantee outperformance.
claims.indicator: correlation vs return tracking of replicator to SG CTA index
claims.testable: yes - compare correlation and cumulative return gap

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: yields reverted that was one move um the JPY rallied I guess on the uh I guess an intervention risk expectations
claims.claim: Early May 2024 trend programs lost on a yield reversal, a yen rally on intervention risk, a dip in energy longs and a cocoa reversal, with no common fundamental cause.
claims.indicator: trend losses in rates, JPY, energy, cocoa
claims.testable: partly - trend P&L by sector in May 2024

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: the btp 50 is down 2.66% for May still up 8.18 for the year soen CTA index down 3% for May
claims.claim: As of mid-May 2024 BTOP50 was down 2.66% for the month and up 8.18% YTD, SG CTA down 3%, and SG Trend down 3.7%, while the S&P 500 total return was up 3.58% in May.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, S&P 500 total return

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the only sector that's up so far this month is is equities and the rest is down
claims.claim: In early May 2024 only equities were positive in trend programs, so the month was a worse than average down month for trend, though the year stayed strong.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: should signal Direction
claims.claim: A listener asks whether signal direction should always dominate signal strength in portfolio construction, e.g. long a strong-signal asset and slightly short a correlated weak-signal asset to cut volatility.
claims.indicator: trend signal direction vs signal strength
claims.testable: yes - compare pure trend vs agnostic risk parity

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: I observe two markets very high correlation
claims.claim: A mean-variance optimizer would long the stronger and short the slightly weaker of two 95%-correlated markets and lever the tiny spread, creating a high-Sharpe-looking relative value trade that is fragile to the signal ordering reversing.
claims.conditions: breaks if the weaker market outperforms (e.g. NASDAQ vs S&P)

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: heavily heavily heavily dependent on those signals playing out exactly as they were observed
claims.claim: Relative value positions built from small signal differentials depend entirely on forecast persistence, create concentrated positions and are arguably no longer trend following.
claims.indicator: RV trades levered from trend signal spread

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: allocate equal units of risk across all the dimensions of a principal component analysis
claims.claim: CFM's agnostic risk parity allocates equal risk across all principal components of the asset correlation matrix, blending the market component (long both) with a small relative value spread component.
claims.indicator: PCA of correlation matrix; equal risk across eigen-portfolios
claims.direction: hold market exposure plus small RV
claims.testable: yes - PCA risk allocation is implementable

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: to the extent that we move away from a binary signal we're implicitly introducing some sort of crosssectional
claims.claim: Scaling positions by signal strength instead of binary already introduces cross-sectional tilts (more contracts in the stronger of two correlated markets) without forcing shorts.
claims.testable: partly - measure cross-sectional share of returns

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there's too much dependence on noise as well as concentration risk
claims.claim: Grossing up the signal differential in a pure relative value trade has too much dependence on noise and concentration, so the middle ground or pure trend direction is preferable.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: any waiting scheme we apply between as a class or between markets even if it's not explicit it has an implied expectation of return
claims.claim: Any fixed weighting scheme (e.g. 60/40, equal risk across asset classes) carries an implied return forecast and a built-in value bet because it sells winners and buys losers to rebalance.
claims.indicator: fixed weights / inverse volatility across asset classes

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: doing one over VA in principle between as a classes implicitly suggests that I expect all of them to deliver the same sharp ratio
claims.claim: Inverse-volatility weights across asset classes imply equal expected Sharpe ratios across them.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: allocating risk where the opportunity lies is prudent
claims.claim: Allocating risk dynamically across asset classes toward where trends exist (e.g. skipping equities in 2022, moving from commodities to the dollar) is more prudent than fixed risk budgets.
claims.indicator: dynamic risk allocation across asset classes
claims.testable: partly - compare dynamic vs equal risk budget

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: by Dollar allocating equal units because simply they happen to have the same Vault I'm ignoring the fact that they are actually correlated
claims.claim: Scaling positions by volatility alone leaves highly correlated clusters over-represented and loosely correlated markets under-represented; correct risk balance needs correlations, not just volatility.
claims.indicator: volatility scaling vs correlation-aware risk contribution
claims.direction: downscale dollar exposure of correlated clusters

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: giving the same the same opportunity set is not the same as saying they we have the same risk allocation at all times
claims.claim: Trend managers give every market the same opportunity, risking the same amount only when trend strength is the same, rather than forcing equal risk by sector.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: forcing some risk budgets in itself implies expectation of returns
claims.claim: Forcing fixed risk budgets (including risk parity) embeds an expectation of equal Sharpe ratios; dynamic budgets avoid that by not forcing allocation into non-trending markets.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if you have Trend following and maybe other liquid assets you would do 100% Trend following
claims.claim: Mathematically, a pure long-term return maximiser would hold close to 100% trend versus 60/40, but institutions' tracking error and career risk against the policy portfolio mean there is no single optimal allocation.
claims.testable: partly - allocation backtest vs policy portfolio

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: a simple 50% S&P and 50% done actually outperforms even you know even our own returns
claims.claim: A 50% S&P 500 and 50% Dunn trend mix historically beat either alone because correlation benefits lift compounding.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: they also admitted to saying well if we if we just looked at our analysis we would have to pitch to our clients a much much higher allocation
claims.claim: Three large consultants said their analysis implied a trend allocation of 45 to 50%, far above what clients accept.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: before 2020 part of the reason why Trend following was not necessarily delivering returns in line with history was the you know the increased fundamental certainty and subdued fundamental disagreement
claims.claim: Trend following works better when investors disagree about fundamental value (post-2020 inflation uncertainty widens views, so price moves carry more information), and worse under consensus valuation where shocks revert.
claims.testable: partly - dispersion of forecasts as proxy

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: if volatility becomes higher and stays High it is more likely that a big move is followed by another big move in the same direction
claims.claim: Volatility clustering gives return predictability without serial correlation, so trend following should do better in high-volatility regimes for a given asset.
claims.testable: yes - trend Sharpe conditional on vol regime

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it is rather that the volatility itself is serly correla in clusters
claims.claim: A price process can look trending with zero serial correlation when volatility clusters and creates skewness, and this alone supports trend following.
claims.testable: yes - simulate clustered vol with iid returns

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it's actually the lower volatile assets between them that have historically delivered stronger RS and we're talking about duration here
claims.claim: High volatility is not a necessary condition for strong trend results: among conventional asset classes lower-volatility assets such as bond duration have historically delivered stronger trend Sharpe ratios.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: alternative markets might have a very more might have a very segregated Marketplace between you know talk about you know some of those alternative commodity markets segregate Market between producers consumers as well as
claims.claim: Segregated markets with persistent producer, consumer and speculator imbalances (alternative commodities) can produce trending behaviour without needing high volatility.
claims.indicator: hedger/speculator imbalance in niche commodity markets

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: when there is more volatility in inflation that seems to have an impact on trending opportunities in many different
claims.claim: Higher inflation volatility has created trending opportunities across many markets compared with the stable low-inflation era, but higher market volatility does not always mean better trend performance.
claims.testable: yes - trend returns vs inflation volatility

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: trend is about a univariate movement that a market that is appreciating continues whereas momentum is more of a
claims.claim: Trend is univariate (an appreciating market continues), whereas momentum is cross-sectional (relative winners keep beating relative losers regardless of sign).

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it's by far the largest performance that Equity momentum has had at least for the last 20 25 years
claims.claim: Q1 2024 US equity momentum, driven by AI stocks such as Nvidia, was its best three-month stretch in 20 to 25 years, roughly double the second best, and index concentration rose with it.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: the more it performs the more we want to buy the same names that have been performing and the more we're buying them the higher they go
claims.claim: Equity momentum is a self-reinforcing positive feedback loop that concentrates portfolios, and hedge funds held record exposure to the momentum factor, explicitly or implicitly.
claims.indicator: hedge fund exposure to momentum factor

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it's very very hard to time that
claims.claim: Timing the end of a crowded equity momentum rally is very hard, so options are limited to managing exposure.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: there is there's an early stage crowding requirement for the trade to uh I guess take off
claims.claim: Like a party, a momentum trade needs early crowding to take off and catalysts such as leverage keep it going, but once crowded it relies on continued inflows.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it's actually the fear of a redemption in other words the risk that is associated with a tactical decision to get out of a trade
claims.claim: Momentum traders know the crash risk but stay in because of fear of missing out and redemption risk for asset managers competing for capital.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: something very endogenous like no funding liquidity is not there anymore and credit lines basically say look you've you've you know you you've grossed out your portfolio as much as you could
claims.claim: A momentum crash can be endogenous: when funding liquidity and credit lines are exhausted at maximum gross exposure, forced selling begins.

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: by Vol scaling your exposure into Equity momentum you kind of reduce your participation when its own volatility increases
claims.claim: Volatility-scaling equity momentum exposure cuts participation when its volatility rises, a prudent way to stay in the trade while reducing crash risk.
claims.indicator: equity momentum factor with volatility scaling
claims.direction: reduce exposure when momentum volatility rises

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: those losing stocks that are far away from the recent Highs are the ones that typically rebound more than the rest
claims.claim: Within a momentum crash, losing stocks far below their recent highs rebound most, so avoiding them on the short side or hedging them reduces crash losses.
claims.indicator: distance from recent high among losers

claims.speaker: Nick Baltas
claims.quote: it's ultimately a liquidity discussion at theend the day right how quickly can we get out
claims.claim: Momentum unwinds are liquidity events: crowded exits cause fire sales and short squeezes, and gross exposure data may hint at a turning point, though calling it is very hard.
claims.indicator: hedge fund gross exposure and momentum positioning
claims.testable: partly - positioning data observable, timing unreliable

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: if you have dynamic position sizing once the thing gets crazy we're going to be scaling out and leave the party
claims.claim: Trend followers with dynamic position sizing scale out when a market goes volatile, which naturally reduces exposure to crowded blow-off moves.

claims.speaker: Neils Kostrup Larsen
claims.quote: cocoa exposure has been dialed down before the downturn came just because the spike up was
claims.claim: Cocoa positions were already reduced before the reversal because the volatility spike weakened the vol-normalised signal even as price kept rising.
